transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-10-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Tara Nguyen (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CTO - NexaHealth), Ben Turner (Platform Engineer), Sofia Lee (Security)

[00:00] Tara: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is the weekly POC check-in, happy Friday. quick roll call?
[00:06] Aisha: Yes, this is Aisha, hi.
[00:07] Ben: Ben here.
[00:08] Sofia: Sofia on security.
[00:10] Tara: Great. Marco from Redwood?
[00:12] Marco: Hey all, Marco Silva, SE. I'll go through the perf notes and runbook items.

[00:22] Tara: Agenda - quick status on onboarding (VPC peering, SSO, KMS), review the first week of pilot results we saw on embeddings/qa latency, share tuning ideas and then agree next steps and owners.

[00:35] Aisha: Sounds good. High level, we want to confirm we can meet the latency SLOs for our clinical triage flow, and that data never leaves our VPC. So the VPC peering + KMS stuff is kinda blocking for us.

[00:49] Marco: Understood. On our side we provisioned the dedicated test pool - it's live but waiting on peering to hit full end-to-end. We did run some local emulated runs with similar inputs and saw median L1 latency around 280ms for 512-token prompts on the g5-like instances. caveat: that was in Redwood hosted staging.

[01:15] Ben: Right, so the peering request we sent through tickets: is there a recommended CIDR? Our infra team wants a small /28 for the peering.

[01:24] Marco: We generally ask for a /24 but /28 can work if it's not colliding. we'll check the network team note - I think Tara, you have the peering docs link?

[01:31] Tara: Yes, sending link in chat - but to summarize: recommended is a /24, but we can accept /28 if you open the 10.10.0.0/28 range and allow the outbound ports we list. I'll put exact firewall rules in the doc.

[01:47] Sofia: For KMS: our mandate is that keys are customer-managed and we need to see the audit logs from Redwood about who requested encryption operations. Is that supported?

[01:56] Marco: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS and we emit a timeline of audit logs. caveat: the logs go to the control plane which in Private Deploys stays in your VPC; for dedicated pilot we can configure logs to your splunk/siem via secure sink. Sometimes the names for services get mixed up in docs, but functionally yes.

[02:15] Sofia: Okay I need the exact field names and retention periods. We have a 7-year retention policy for some keys.

[02:23] Marco: I'll add the log schema plus retention options to the security pack. Tara will ship the pack after the call.

[02:31] Tara: Yep, I'll share the pack with SOC2 excerpts and KMS integration notes.

[02:36] Aisha: Good. On the pilot results - Ben shared the dashboard earlier, we saw a spike in p99 on Wednesday; can you walk through what might cause that?

[02:46] Marco: Sure. Quick context: the test had a bursty load from your eval harness around 2am UTC and a few requests hit >1k tokens due to a chat continuity test. That's when we saw p99 climb to ~1.8s. Baseline medians were ~300ms for standard requests. We suspect KV-cache misses + a longer seq-length combo.

[03:10] Ben: The harness was re-playing production-ish sessions to test context windows. We can tune to limit sequence lengths but we'd like to understand real-world behavior.

[03:19] Marco: Two levers: (1) prefix KV caching - we can prewarm caches for known conversation patterns, (2) quantization / model variant - moving to a quantized variant dropped per-token time in our internal runs by roughly 15-20% but at small quality delta.

[03:36] Aisha: Hmm quality delta is a concern for clinical language. We can't accept hallucinations. How do we measure that?

[03:42] Marco: We recommend a small eval set from you - 200-500 prompts - and run automated quality checks (BLEU-ish / n-gram overlap isn't perfect for LLMs but we use a domain-specific scoring + human review). we'll push recommended thresholds in the eval template.

[03:57] Tara: Also Redwood Optimize will give suggestions on batching and quantization based on observed traffic. That can help keep cost down while meeting quality SLOs.

[04:06] Sofia: On the security side, we need to confirm data residency - will logs or any model-hosted traces leave the EU region? we're EU-first.

[04:14] Marco: The dedicated pool was provisioned in eu-west-1 per your request. The control plane metadata (alerts/usage) can be routed to your region; we will not replicate PII outside region. I'll confirm the retention behavior in the pack.

[04:29] Ben: Quick infra question - for the peering, do we need to enable any egress rules for health checks to Redwood?

[04:34] Marco: Just allow outbound to the small set of Redwood control plane IPs (listed in doc). Health checks use TLS on 443 and a couple of ephemeral ports. I'll put the exact IPs and ports.

[04:45] Tara: Switching to perf tunings - Marco, can you summarize the run you'd propose next week?

[04:50] Marco: Sure. Plan: run a 4k-token throughput test hitting your real harness, 10k requests over 2 hours, measure median/p95/p99 and token-per-second, compare baseline quantized vs fp16 variant. Also we'll test a prewarm with KV cache and a run without to show delta. We'll need Ben to enable a peered route + open firewall so dedicated pool can talk to harness.

[05:12] Ben: I can do that. I'll schedule a maintenance window and provide CIDRs.

[05:17] Aisha: Timeline - if the perf run looks good and security sign-off is reasonable, we want to move to a 30-day dedicated pilot. What's the pricing posture?

[05:25] Tara: We'll send an estimated dedicated pilot pricing sheet - it will include reserved GPU hours, overflow/burst cost, and a recommended size for the pool based on the perf run. Expect to see a monthly estimate within 2 business days.

[05:35] Sofia: On legal - we have a few contract redlines around data retention and subprocessing; our legal team will send the markups. Any standard SLAs for dedicated pilots?

[05:43] Tara: We can include a pilot SLA: 99.5% uptime for the dedicated pool, plus support response times for P1/P2. For enterprise we have stronger SLAs but for pilots we try to be flexible.

[05:56] Ben: One more: we saw a couple of labeled mis-attributions in the initial transcript when we reviewed the demo recording; might be Fireflies but also the model sometimes mislabels medical entity names. Any suggestions?

[06:07] Marco: For NER stability, we recommend a light post-processing classifier tuned to your entity set - that reduces false-positives. we can demo a small pipeline we use for customers.

[06:18] Aisha: Okay great. On data - will Redwood persist raw request payloads by default? We'd prefer redaction or not persisting to control plane for compliance.

[06:26] Marco: By default we keep traces for 30 days but for dedicated/private we can turn off request persistence or redact PII fields at ingestion. We'll show the config in the security pack.

[06:36] Sofia: Please include the exact API flags to turn persistence off. I want to give that to my compliance engineer.

[06:41] Marco: Noted. I'll include an example curl and policy.

[06:44] Tara: Let's recap action items and owners quickly.

[06:47] Tara: Marco will run the 4k-token perf test and deliver results; Ben will provide CIDR and open firewall rules; Tara will send security pack and pricing estimate; Sofia will validate KMS requirements.

[06:59] Aisha: Do we have a proposed date for the perf run?

[07:02] Marco: How about next Thursday 2026-10-28?

[07:05] Ben: Works for me, I'll block time and do the peering ahead of that.

[07:09] Tara: Okay. I'll follow up in email with the pricing sheet and attach the security pack.

[07:14] Sofia: Quick question - competitor note: our security team asked if you integrate with Anthropic or OpenAI for fallback calls.

[07:21] Marco: We support routing policies but for this dedicated pilot we recommend keeping requests in your private pool; fallback to third-party services is configurable but we can disable it by policy.

[07:33] Aisha: Perfect. Anything else?

[07:36] Ben: No from infra.

[07:37] Sofia: Nothing more.

[07:38] Tara: Great, thanks everyone. We'll send notes and items.

[07:41] Aisha: Thanks.

[07:43] Meeting ends.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional speaker mislabels and minor transcription errors present (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cache" in two places). References: security pack link (to be shared), perf spreadsheet (internal redwood link), peering docs (link sent in chat).
